newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends off highs, weather concerns ease.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends off highs, weather concerns ease.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended higher on Tuesday, but sharply off peaks, after the latest Brazilian weather forecasts reduced the chances of crop-damaging cold this weekend, traders said.

Early in the session, weather-related buying drove the benchmark September contract to a high of 184.50 cents per lb, before nerves were unruffled. September closed at 175.25 cents, up 2.85 cents. It reached a low of 173.00 cents.
Spot July finished 4.10 cents higher, at 196.50 cents, while the outer months closed up 2.25 to 3.34.
The July/September switch widened to 21.25 cents, from 20.00 cents at the close on Monday, while September/December narrowed to 20.90 cents compared with 21.50 cents.

Brazilian metereologist Somar said on Tuesday afternoon that Brazil's coffee belt now looked much less likely to see damaging cold over the weekend, with a large polar air mass breaking into two smaller masses.
On Monday, Somar said the air mass could represent the greatest threat of frost seen so far this year.
"Everyone was watching the weather," said South Futures president Stephen Smith. "When Somar came out and downgraded the frost threat, everyone said: 'Get me out'."
Smith said news that Brazil's key port of Santos was partially paralyzed by an indefinite strike involving a group of administrative workers lent some support to the market.

Although the strike, which began today at 0100 local/0400 GMT today according to a CODESP port authority spokesman, affected ships loading sugar and soymeal, traders feared it might eventually impact coffee shipments.
But traders said a build up in stocks certified for delivery against the exchange -- as well as an increase in stocks pending certification -- could weigh on the market.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 1,783 60-kg bags as of June 30, to 49,900 bags. There were 27,313 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Technically, traders said the high of 184.50-185.00 cents basis September would provide nearby resistance, followed by 192.00. Support was pegged at the session low of 173.00 cents, they said.
Volume was moderate, at an estimated 7,167 lots.
